summary: Intermittent 504s and high tail latency for long streaming completions due to APIGW buffering + upstream send_timeout
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors and elevated 95th/99th percentile latency on streaming completion endpoints when generating long outputs (>10k tokens). Impact: blocking production workflows for BrightAdopt personalization pipelines; visible as spikes in user-facing latency and a small fraction (~0.6%) of requests failing with 504 over the last 48h. Environment: Hosted Redwood API, production us-east deployment, customer pinned to gpt-redwood-13b-v2. Note: traffic uses long-lived HTTP/1.1 connections routed through our edge ALB -> nginx reverse-proxy -> serving runtime. Hypothesis: APIGW/ALB proxy buffering plus upstream nginx send_timeout or proxy_send_timeout is causing backpressure during slow incremental streaming writes (small chunk sizes), triggering a hard cutoff (504) after idle period even though backend is still generating tokens.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's call pattern: streaming completion with max_tokens=10000, small chunking (stream chunk every 150-300ms), persistent connection reuse from same client IP.
2) Send requests to /v1/completions with pinned model gpt-redwood-13b-v2 from us-east region.
3) Observe tail latency metrics in Console: 95th/99th token latency increases and occasional 504s logged on apigw within 2-5 minutes of sustained streaming traffic.
4) Reproduce by running a 500-request load test with same chunk cadence; failures reproduce at ~0.5-1% of requests.
5) Toggle client-side keepalive to shorter interval (<10s) and observe reduced failure rate (customer reports workaround).

investigation_notes: 03/12 19:05 - Support initial triage: correlated error spikes with customer's request pattern. No config changes on customer side in window.

03/12 19:40 - SRE inspected ALB logs: 504s show backend reported as healthy and returned chunks before the 504 timestamp (backend 200 then apigw 504). Pattern consistent with buffering/idle detection downstream of ALB.

03/12 20:15 - Ran controlled replay using customer's trace headers. Reproduced 504s when chunk cadence >150ms and chunk size <1KB, especially when correlation-id header grows large (trace propagation adds ~600-1200 bytes).

03/12 21:00 - Hypothesis: ALB or internal edge proxy switches to buffered mode when headers exceed threshold or when it detects small chunked responses; buffered mode interacts poorly with nginx's proxy_send_timeout or the edge connection idle detection, causing a 30s+ idle window where ALB triggers a 504 despite backend continuing to produce small chunks.

03/13 09:30 - Verified nginx 'proxy_send_timeout' default was 60s on the edge-layer; in buffered mode, the proxy may wait for buffer to fill, delaying writes to client and allowing idle timers to fire.
comments: Lena Ortiz (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported spike in 99th percentile latency and intermittent 504s; they are enterprise tier and in production. Assigned to SRE for deeper tracing.
Marco Chen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally with customer's headers. Filing for further kernel-level logs and nginx config audit. Adding components apigw and edge-proxy.

BrightAdopt (Customer) 2026-03-12: We see the same behavior. We observed that switching client keepalives to 8s reduces failures. Happy to provide sample request traces and packet captures if that helps.

Marco Chen (SRE) 2026-03-13: Requested TEMP workaround: reduce client chunk interval or reduce header bloat (disable per-token tracing header) while we evaluate. Also testing a config change to reduce nginx proxy_send_timeout to 30s for streaming routes to see impact on tail latency.
Lena Ortiz (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer accepted workaround and is testing in staging. Marked follow-up for config rollouts and runbook updates.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14 - Temporary mitigation: advised customer to reduce client chunk cadence (<100ms) or disable per-token tracing header to keep header sizes small. This reduced observed failure rate in staging to <0.05%.

2026-03-14 - Engineering fix in progress: change deployment to disable APIGW response buffering for streaming endpoints and lower nginx proxy_send_timeout for streaming routes. PR opened: edge-proxy#842. Will rollout to canary in us-east on 2026-03-15.

2026-03-14 - Follow-ups: update streaming runbook, add synthetic test that mimics small-chunk streaming with large headers to detect regressions, and notify customers who use long-running streaming to follow best-practices for header size and chunk cadence.
2026-03-14 - Status: Workaround validated by customer; Engineering deployment scheduled; ticket will be closed after canary verification and post-deploy monitoring for 48h.
